notes.text: Identity is legal-entity based and every counted listing is proved by a verbatim span copied out of a securities filing that was actually fetched and text-extracted in this run, not from a search snippet. The exchange field carries the exchange name exactly as the filing prints it, which is why it reads 'New York Stock Exchange' rather than the NYSE shorthand used in earlier maps: the excerpt has to state the exchange the listing claims, and inventing a shorthand the source never used would break that. One disclosure a later audit needs: sec.gov and data.sec.gov both return HTTP 403 to this venue, so most of these filings were opened through a third-party document mirror rather than the regulator's own host. The document at each URL is the registrant's own Form 10-K or Form 20-F and every excerpt was text-extracted from the fetched file, but the host is a mirror and the audit should re-open these URLs on that understanding.

What this census cannot see, stated plainly. This chain is 61 percent non-US by ticker, and the official identity sources for those listings are the ones that defeat automated reading: sec.gov, data.sec.gov, nyse.com, hkex.com.hk, londonstockexchange.com company pages, nseindia.com, tmx.com and the JPX client portal all returned either HTTP 403 or a JavaScript shell with no instrument record in it. Euronext returned a page without the symbol field. The only official listing source that survived at scale was the securities filing itself, which biases this run's completed coverage toward SEC registrants. Eleven of the thirteen links are therefore left OPEN rather than closed: OPEN here means the census is genuinely incomplete, not that the universe is small. The links that need non-US identity work first are hydroprocessing-catalysts, the money corner, which holds one issuer where the real universe also contains BASF, Clariant, Johnson Matthey, Sinopec and JGC; and shipyard-newbuild-capacity and refinery-capacity-response, which have no placements at all because every credible name on them is Korean, Chinese, Japanese or Indian.

russian-refining-attrition is the one link that is genuinely closed, and it closes at zero. That is not a gap in the search: the chain's own note says the ticker list is deliberately empty because Rosneft, Lukoil, Gazprom Neft and Surgutneftegas are sanctioned, and the search record proves it from two independent directions, an official exchange suspension notice and a dated sanctions analysis. The link that sets demand for the whole chain has no instrument, which is exactly the ARCH-003-inverted shape the chain already names.

Both rows stay OPEN, because OPEN here is the honest reading: the real universe on each link is larger than what this run could prove, so EXHAUSTED would be a lie about the world rather than a statement about the census. Four channels answered this venue and are worth recording for the next run: the BSE corporate filings archive at bseindia.com, which serves SEBI LODR letters whose headers print the legal issuer, the exchange and the NSE symbol together; HKEXnews at hkexnews.hk, whose announcement covers print the exchange disclaimer, the legal name and the stock code on one page; Japanese earnings reports hosted on the issuer's own investor site, whose header block prints listed company name, listed exchange and stock code; and issuer hosted SEBI filings such as BPCL's own results letter.

What this pass still cannot see, named issuer by issuer so the gap is falsifiable. shipyard-newbuild-capacity is dominated by Korea and by China's A share yards, and neither could be admitted.
